title: Four cells of a segmenting egg never meet in a point; a polar furrow is always present

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Four cells of a segmenting egg never meet in a point; a polar furrow is always present

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the four-celled stage of a segmenting egg whose cells are in full fluid contact, the four cells cannot meet in a single point; a short intermediate partition (the polar furrow) must be present, and reports of four cells meeting in a simple cross are due to error or imperfect observation.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: it is quite certain that no simple and homogeneous system of fluid films such as we are dealing with is in equilibrium without its presence.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates”; topic “Polar furrow in four-celled eggs”. Scope: four-celled stage of segmenting eggs of animals in which blastomeres are in full fluid contact

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch07-05: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.84

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The universal topological prediction is exceptionally clear and refuted by a verified four-way full-contact junction. Existing 3D embryo datasets and standard surface reconstruction can test it across several taxa.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reconstruct four-cell embryos in 3D and test whether any full-contact configuration has a four-way junction rather than an intervening polar furrow.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The full-fluid-contact condition must be distinguished from partial adhesion.

Some species and imaging orientations are underrepresented.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Presence or absence of a polar furrow is a yes-or-no observation, and public cleavage images of frog, sea urchin and other embryos are sufficient to make it. Three-dimensional sets remove the viewing-angle error the claim says produced reports of a simple cross. Coverage is uneven across phyla, but it is enough to confirm or refute the pattern in eggs whose blastomeres meet in full contact.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In four-cell embryos whose blastomeres are in full contact, score whether a polar furrow is present or the four cells meet at one point. A short intermediate partition in essentially every such embryo would support the claim; stable four-way crosses in fully apposed fluid blastomeres would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Molluscs and annelids, classical material for this stage, are less completely archived than frog and sea urchin.

A cross seen in a single optical plane can hide a short polar furrow, so only 3D or time-resolved volumes are decisive.
